Rebuild a weighted sample from its rows

Source: R/state.R
as_drawn.Rd

A weighted sample carries its design, a copy of its frame and its inclusion probabilities as attributes. A CSV or spreadsheet file, a database table and merge() keep none of them, so ht_total(), ht_mean(), as_svydesign() and sample_summary() refuse the rows that come back. as_drawn() puts the attributes back. It matches each row of data to its row of frame, works out the inclusion probabilities again from design, and sets .prob, .weight and .row as draw() sets them.

Usage

as_drawn(data, design, frame, by = NULL)

Arguments

data

The sampled rows as read back: a data frame with the .row column draw() added, or with the id column or columns named in by.

design

The design the sample was drawn with.

frame

The data frame the sample was drawn from, as it was then.

by

NULL to match rows through .row, or the names of one or more columns of data and frame that identify a frame row.

Value

A data frame of the class of data, ready for ht_total(), ht_mean(), as_svydesign() and sample_summary().

Matching rows to the frame

With by = NULL, each row is matched through its .row column, the frame row draw() recorded for it. frame must then be the frame the sample was drawn from, with its rows in the same order. A frame in another order, such as a database table read without ORDER BY, holds other rows at those positions, and its strata and clusters would be wrong for the sample. Each column data shares with frame is therefore compared with the frame rows .row names, and a column whose values differ is refused. Numbers need to agree to about eight significant digits, fewer than a CSV file keeps, and a number read back from text, such as "007", is compared as the number 7. Text such as "T", "F", "t" or "f" that a file gave back as a logical column is compared as TRUE or FALSE, as readr::read_csv() reads it. A date-time read back in another time zone agrees when it is the same instant or shows the same clock time, since readr::read_csv() and data.table::fread() read the clock time a CSV file holds as UTC. A missing value on either side is not compared, so a frame column that fieldwork fills in is accepted. Nor is a date that a file gave back as text, whose format a spreadsheet may have changed. A column changed after the draw, such as a corrected address, is refused too; rename it in data, or match on an id. A data that shares no column with frame besides those draw() adds cannot be checked, so keep an id column in the file.

With by, rows are matched on the values of one or more id columns that data and frame share. Values are compared as match() compares them, and as text when the two columns have different classes, so an id stored as "007" does not match the number 7 that a CSV file gives back.

When data has both .row and the by columns, they must agree. A frame row found through by that is not the one .row names means frame is not in the order it had when the sample was drawn, which changes the probabilities of designs that depend on that order, such as design_systematic(); the rebuild is refused.

A row with a missing id, an id that appears twice in data, an id that frame does not have or holds more than once, and a row the design gives a probability of 0 are refused, with the ids named.

Every row drawn

data must hold every row that was drawn, with or without a fieldwork result. A subset, such as the rows that responded, is not a sample from the design, and its standard errors would be wrong. For a design that draws a fixed number of rows (simple, stratified, spread, temporal, spatial and reservoir designs, systematic designs given n, and design_weighted() with method = "systematic", alone or as the rest of design_certainty()), a data with another number of rows is refused. A design_cluster() or design_multistage() sample, also as the rest of design_certainty(), is refused when its rows are not of n_clusters clusters or a cluster does not hold the rows the design takes from it, which are all of its rows for whole clusters, and the same number from each cluster when that number does not depend on which clusters were selected. A design weighted conditional on its clusters (see "Design weights" in draw()) is rebuilt from the clusters its rows belong to, which must hold the rows the design takes from each given that selection. A frame row the design takes with certainty, with probability 1, is in every sample, and a data without it is refused whatever the design. Keep the rows with no response, with y missing, and estimate a mean with ht_mean(na_rm = TRUE); see "Missing values and nonresponse" in ht_total().

A list from a design with reserve is rebuilt whole, the main sample and every reserve, with the .reserve column draw() added, which records the order the reserves are used in. Pass the result to use_reserves().

What comes back

The rows of data in their own order, with .prob, .weight and .row first and the other columns of data after them. .prob and .weight come from design. A numeric .prob in data must agree with them, or the design or the frame is not the one the sample was drawn with. A .weight adjusted after the draw is replaced by 1 / .prob, so the adjustment has to be made again.

Strata, clusters and the other design columns are read from the copy of frame stored with the result, as for a sample from draw(), so data needs only the columns to estimate from: y and the by columns of the estimates. add_fieldwork() joins results that come back keyed by an id.

See also

add_fieldwork() to join fieldwork results, compact_sample() to drop frame columns before saving or sharing a sample, and draw().

Examples

pop <- data.frame(id = 1:200, site = rep(c("a", "b"), times = c(150, 50)))
by_site <- design_stratified("site", n = 40)
s <- draw(pop, by_site, seed = 1, weights = TRUE)

# A file keeps the rows and loses the design
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
write.csv(s, path, row.names = FALSE)
back <- as_drawn(read.csv(path), by_site, pop)
sample_summary(back)
#> Sample of 40 from 200  (stratified design)
#>   sampling fraction  0.2
#>   design weights     5 to 5   (cv 0)
#>   effective n        40  (Kish, from the weights alone)
#>   rebuilt            by as_drawn() of drawn 0.2.0.9000 on 2026-11-17; the seed is not recorded
#> 
#>   by site:
#>     group  drawn  in frame   rate
#>     a         30      150  0.200
#>     b         10       50  0.200

# Without `.row`, match on an id column
ids <- read.csv(path)[, c("id", "site")]
back <- as_drawn(ids, by_site, pop, by = "id")
unlink(path)
